The lines x−12=y+1−1=z3\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{3}2x−1​=−1y+1​=3z​ and x−3−4=y+22=z−3−6\dfrac{x-3}{-4} = \dfrac{y+2}{2} = \dfrac{z-3}{-6}−4x−3​=2y+2​=−6z−3​ are:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Lines with proportional DRs are parallel; if they also share a point, they coincide.

  1. 1

    Compare the DRs 2,−1,32, -1, 32,−1,3 and −4,2,−6-4, 2, -6−4,2,−6.

    −42=2−1=−63=−2  ⇒  the lines are parallel\dfrac{-4}{2} = \dfrac{2}{-1} = \dfrac{-6}{3} = -2 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{the lines are parallel}2−4​=−12​=3−6​=−2⇒the lines are parallel−42=2−1=−63=−2  ⇒  the lines are parallel\displaystyle \dfrac{-4}{2} = \dfrac{2}{-1} = \dfrac{-6}{3} = -2 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{the lines are parallel}2−4​=−12​=3−6​=−2⇒the lines are parallel
  2. 2

    Check whether the point (3,−2,3)(3, -2, 3)(3,−2,3) of the second line lies on the first.

    3−12=−2+1−1=33=1  ✓\dfrac{3-1}{2} = \dfrac{-2+1}{-1} = \dfrac{3}{3} = 1 \;\checkmark23−1​=−1−2+1​=33​=1✓3−12=−2+1−1=33=1  ✓\displaystyle \dfrac{3-1}{2} = \dfrac{-2+1}{-1} = \dfrac{3}{3} = 1 \;\checkmark23−1​=−1−2+1​=33​=1✓
    1
  3. 3

    Parallel lines with a common point coincide. Hence the answer is option (B).

Answer(B) coincident

Watch out Choosing "parallel but not coincident" (option A) without checking for a common point.

Verify that the lines given by r⃗=(1−λ)i^+(λ−2)j^+(3−2λ)k^\vec{r} = (1 - \lambda)\hat{i} + (\lambda - 2)\hat{j} + (3 - 2\lambda)\hat{k}r=(1−λ)i^+(λ−2)j^​+(3−2λ)k^ and r⃗=(μ+1)i^+(2μ−1)j^−(2μ+1)k^\vec{r} = (\mu + 1)\hat{i} + (2\mu - 1)\hat{j} - (2\mu + 1)\hat{k}r=(μ+1)i^+(2μ−1)j^​−(2μ+1)k^ are skew lines. Hence, find the shortest distance between the lines.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea d=∣(b⃗1×b⃗2)⋅(a⃗2−a⃗1)∣b⃗1×b⃗2∣∣d = \left|\dfrac{(\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) \cdot (\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1)}{|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2|}\right|d=​∣b1​×b2​∣(b1​×b2​)⋅(a2​−a1​)​​; lines are skew if not parallel and d≠0d \neq 0d=0.
